verdicts.question: What are the exact 8-digit ITC-HS lines for glass cullet (7001), lead scrap (7802), the 8549 sub-headings (lithium-ion cells, dry cells, CRT glass, circuit boards) and textiles (6309/6310)? Which E-Waste Rules 2022 schedule item codes (ITEW, CEEW, LSEEW numbers) match phones, laptops, TVs, fridges, washing machines and ACs?
verdicts.problems: Verification blocked: WebSearch budget exhausted (200/200) and page fetches refused, so none of the ten cited sources (CPCB gazette copy, CPCB FAQ, DGCI&S CHP_70.pdf, Eximguru, Busy, Eximpe) was confirmed by any snippet; every figure is 'not confirmed by snippet'. Internal consistency: the 8549 structure (11 lines, 854911/12/13/14/19, 21/29, 31/39, 91/99) matches the HS 2022 heading text as I know it; the 7001 (70010010/20/90), 7802 (78020010 ISRI grades / 78020090 other), 6309 (63090000) and 6310 (four 631010 sorted + five 631090 unsorted lines) layouts match the Indian tariff as I know it; the E-Waste Rules 2022 facts (G.S.R. 801(E), 2 Nov 2022, in force 1 Apr 2023, 106 items in 7 categories) and the codes ITEW3/ITEW15/CEEW1–CEEW4/CEEW6/LSEEW14/LSEEW9/LSEEW20/LSEEW21 match Schedule I as I recall it, but ITEW24 (UPS), ITEW25 (inverter), LSEEW33 (kettles), 'Gazette No. 713' and the 8-digit descriptions taken from trade mirrors are unverified. Substantive issues: (1) '78020010 is import-policy Free' is misleading without the policy condition: lead scrap and used lead-acid batteries are hazardous waste under the HOWM Rules 2016 (Schedule III/VI), so import needs MoEFCC/SPCB permission and the 'Free' status is subject to that; (2) mapping CRT tube/panel/funnel glass to 85499100 is defensible only while it is 'activated glass' in e-waste form, but bare CRT glass is also arguably 7001 waste glass; the answer notes a customs-broker check, which is right; (3) no newer development checked: HS 2022 remains current (HS 2028 not yet), and the 2023/2024 E-Waste amendments did not change Schedule I as far as I know, but this was not confirmed. Against the refined chain: the answer only codes the S0–S2 raw-scrap end; the pre-processor and recycler outputs in the founder's chain CSV (cold/hot-washed PET flake, rPET/rHDPE/rPP/LDPE granules, recycled pulp, shredded steel, aluminium ingot and dross, copper granules and PVC granules from cable, crumb rubber/TPO/recovered carbon black, lead paste/grids/PP casing, re-refined base oil, furnace-ready cullet, recycled aggregate, shoddy fibre) need their own HS lines because a lot changes heading when it changes state (e.g. PET bottles 39159090 → flake/granule 3907; cable scrap 7404 → copper granules 7404/7403 and PVC granules 3904; tyres 4004 → crumb 40040000 and TPO 2707/2710; paper 4707 → pulp 4706; glass 70010010 stays 7001 as cullet); by-products and residuals in each processing record (dross 2620, fly ash/slag 2618/2619/2621, sludge as hazardous waste) also need codes. So the HS attribute must hang off the lot/state, not the material.
verdicts.correction: Keep the raw-scrap 8-digit lines and Schedule I codes as seeded defaults but mark them 'unverified against CBIC tariff as of 30 Sep 2026' until someone opens taxinformation.cbic.gov.in and the CPCB gazette copy in a browser. Change the data model: attach the ITC-HS line to each lot at its state (S0–S9), not to the material, and seed processed-state lines for every pre-processor/recycler output and by-product in docs/plan/inputs/2026-09-30-founder-research-part-1/refined-roles-material-chains--2-material-process-chains.csv (PET bottle scrap 3915 → PET flake/granule 3907; HDPE/LDPE/PP scrap 3915 → granules 3901/3902; paper 4707 → pulp 4706; ferrous 7204 → shredded 72044900; aluminium 7602 → ingot 7601 with dross 2620; cable 7404 → copper granules 7404/7403 + PVC granules 3904; tyres 4004/4012 → crumb 40040000, TPO 2707/2710, recovered carbon black 2803; lead-acid batteries 85491100 → lead paste/grids 7802/7801, PP casing 3915; glass 70010010 → furnace-ready cullet 70010010; C&D → aggregate 2517; textiles 6309/6310 → shoddy fibre 5104/5505). Add the HOWM Rules caveat to lead: 78020010 import policy is subject to hazardous-waste permission, so no yard should read 'Free' as no-permit. Keep the customs-broker question for populated boards (85493100 vs 85493900) and CRT glass (85499100 vs 70010010). Status should be 'partly' until the tariff lines are confirmed from an official page.

verdicts.question: What words do Bengaluru kabadiwalas use for plastics and other scrap (Delhi's Teri, Phugga, Jhaap, Panni; English PET, PP, HD, LD; Kannada terms)? Is 'gujari' used for scrap shops in Bengaluru? Are milk pouches a separate paid stream? Are small appliances and fans priced per kg or per piece?
verdicts.problems: Verification blocked (search budget exhausted, fetches refused): none of the 17 sources was confirmed by a snippet, so every price and every quotation is 'not confirmed by snippet'. What is consistent with my knowledge: 'gujari' (ಗುಜರಿ) is the everyday Kannada/Bengaluru word for scrap and the scrap shop, the Shivajinagar 'Gujri' market exists, and the Kannada material words (kabbiṇa iron, gāju glass, tāmra copper, hittāḷe brass, raddi for waste paper) are correct. What is unverified and load-bearing: (1) 'Milk Covers ₹0/kg' on The Kabadiwala's Bengaluru list is a single aggregator's page 'read 29 Sep 2026' and could not be confirmed; DWCCs and many gujaris do take rinsed LDPE milk covers as a low-value stream (₹0–₹10/kg), so 'not a paid stream' should be 'often unpaid, sometimes ₹5–10/kg when rinsed and dry' pending the pilot visit; (2) the per-piece prices (LCD TV ₹50, CRT ₹100, laptop ₹250, fridge ₹350/₹550, WM ₹300, AC 1.5 T ₹2,500, 2 T ₹3,000) and the other-site ranges are unconfirmed and are aggregator buy prices, not gujari prices; (3) the KMF corn-starch compostable Nandini pouch 'rolled out across Bengaluru from July 2025' and '20–25 lakh pouches a day' are unconfirmed; a pilot-wide compostable pouch would be a major change and needs a KMF/press confirmation before a separate code is built for it; (4) the Delhi slang (Teri, Phugga, Jhaap) is admitted unverified, correctly. Against the refined chain: per-piece appliances are not a terminal price, they are lots that an e-waste dismantler (pre-processor) splits into a main output and by-products (fridge → compressor with copper windings, steel body, PU foam and refrigerant as residual/hazardous; fan → copper winding, aluminium/steel, plastic); so the unit attribute belongs to the L1/L2 price levels and the piece must convert to kg fractions at S2/S4 with a yield. Milk covers and the compostable pouch also need a destination role: the LDPE cover goes to a DWCC/MRF or film agglomerator (S1 → S4/S7), the compostable pouch must route to wet-waste/composting, never to the plastic chain.
verdicts.correction: Keep 'gujari' and the Kannada material names. Rewrite the rest as pilot-dependent: milk covers are a separate low-value LDPE stream that is often unpaid but sometimes bought at a few rupees per kg when rinsed and dry; verify on the day-one shop visits and let the price be ₹0 or more per shop. Treat all listed per-piece prices as unverified aggregator quotes and re-collect them in the pilot's first week. Keep the compostable Nandini pouch as an open item ('confirm with KMF or a dated press page before building the code') rather than a fact. Model appliances as per-piece lots at L1/L2 that carry a default dismantling yield table (main output, saleable by-products, residual/hazardous fractions such as refrigerant, CRT glass, batteries) so the pre-processor step can create the child lots the founder's chain requires; fans, mixers and irons default to per kg with a per-shop override. Route LDPE milk covers to the DWCC/MRF or film-agglomeration role, and the compostable pouch to the wet-waste role. Status stays 'partly'; whoToAsk unchanged (gujaris across three BBMP zones plus Hasiru Dala DWCC operators).

verdicts.question: Which published source should supply the CO2e emission factor for recycling each material (paper, PET, HDPE, PP, LDPE, ferrous, aluminium, copper, brass, glass, e-waste): CDM AMS-III.AJ, Gold Standard 448, India-specific studies? Who should own an open material-code standard long term (an industry body such as MRAI or IARPMA, a BIS committee, a foundation), and under which licence?
verdicts.problems: Verification blocked (search budget exhausted, fetches refused): none of the 12 sources was confirmed by a snippet, so the AMS-III.AJ default table (1.11 MWh/t + 15 GJ/t PET, 0.83 + 15 HDPE, 1.67 + 15 LDPE, 0.56 + 11.6 PP, 0.026 MWh/t glass), the Bi factors (0.72/0.68/0.56/0.67), the v9.0 adoption date (8 Sep 2022), the CEA v21.0 figures (0.710 weighted average, OM 0.961, BM 0.512, CM 0.736 for FY 2024-25), the Gold Standard 448 date (2 May 2025) and the Tribune 8 July 2026 story are all 'not confirmed by snippet'; the researcher also admits the defaults came from the v08.0 draft, not v9.0. Points that look wrong or stale on their face: (1) 'MRAI is metals-only' is wrong: the Material Recycling Association of India covers ferrous, non-ferrous, paper, plastics, e-waste and tyres, so it can sit on a cross-material steering group; (2) 'US EPA WARM v15 (November 2020) is the most complete public table' is out of date: EPA released WARM Version 16 (late 2023) with revised factors, so any indicative table should be pinned to v16 or say why v15 is used; the v15 figures quoted (corrugated −3.14, newspaper −2.71, mixed paper −3.55, HDPE −0.76, PET −1.04, PP −0.79, aluminium cans −9.13, steel cans −1.83, copper wire −4.49, glass −0.28, mixed electronics −0.79 MTCO2e/short ton) match my recollection of v15 and the 1.1023 short-ton-to-tonne conversion is correct; (3) 'BIS standards are sold, not open' is only half right: BIS gives free online read access to Indian Standards, though the licence is not open; (4) the answer drops PVC even though AMS-III.AJ covers PVC and the founder's chain produces PVC granules from cable stripping; (5) the repo's credits cluster says AMS-III.AJ applies a discount to virgin displacement and that SWM Rules 2026 mandatory recycling raises an additionality problem for any credit claim, which this answer does not mention; (6) 'AMS-III.BA Appendix 1 supplies the Bi factors' and 'brass has no default' were not checked. Against the refined chain: a per-material factor at collection double-counts; the credit must be computed once, at the state transition where recycled feedstock is produced (S7/S9 main output), using each processing record's yield so residual waste and by-products are not credited as recycled tonnes; pre-processor by-products (PP caps, PVC label flake, dross, ASR fluff) need their own treatment (credit, zero or burden), and industrial by-products (fly ash, slag, bagasse) are outside AMS-III.AJ and need other methods (e.g. cement-blending methodologies) or an explicit 'no carbon figure' flag. The licence recommendation (CC BY 4.0 for the spec, Apache-2.0 for schemas/SDKs, avoid NC/SA) is sound and Beckn's CC BY-NC-SA is the right cautionary example, but none of those pages was confirmed either.
verdicts.correction: Method: keep CDM AMS-III.AJ as the backbone but label every default 'from the v08.0 draft, to be re-read against v9.0 in a browser' and add PVC to the covered list; compute the credit once per processing record at the S7/S9 main output using the record's yield (tonnes of recycled feedstock actually produced), with by-products and residual waste credited zero unless a method covers them; pin a factor version and the CEA baseline version on every carbon number; feed the electricity term with the latest CEA CO2 Baseline Database (v21.0 claimed, figure 0.710 tCO2/MWh unverified; anyone can confirm from cea.nic.in in five minutes); use AMS-III.BA for e-waste metals and leave brass and copper cathode as open items; for indicative on-screen numbers use EPA WARM v16 (not v15) and label it 'indicative, US grid'; industrial by-products (fly ash, slag, bagasse, dross) get no recycling credit until a fitting method is chosen. Note the credits cluster's finding that mandatory recycling under SWM Rules 2026 may defeat additionality, so present these as footprint-avoided estimates, not saleable credits. Ownership: publish the code list under CC BY 4.0 with Apache-2.0 schemas now; the future foundation's steering group should seat MRAI as a multi-material body (not metals-only), IARPMA, a plastics body, Hasiru Dala and CPCB/KSPCB as observers; offer the list to BIS as reference input. Status: 'partly'; whoToAsk adds: download AMS-III.AJ v9.0 and CEA v21.0 in a browser and confirm the WARM v16 table before any carbon figure is shown.
